authorization: Director instructed: if Phase 2 goal completed successfully, begin Phase 3; otherwise do not. Phase 2 goal completed successfully with diagnosed limitations.
scope: Isolated production safety core; no production cutover, Phase 4, or complete M1 claim.

safety_policy.unknown_submission: Hold allowance, block potentially duplicate calls, require reconciliation.
safety_policy.known_request: Record ID immediately; reconcile original request using actual provider capabilities. No assumed queue API.
safety_policy.publication: Snapshot exact inspected bytes; persisted intent, non-overwriting content-addressed link, fsync, fenced final commit; reuse or verify replay.
safety_policy.pause: Durable SQL flag blocks new worker actions. Already committed external operations remain in flight; trusted receipts and settlements still record.
safety_policy.operator: Trusted control-plane APIs with auditable decisions; existing interface authentication is a Phase 4 integration requirement.
safety_policy.billing: Integer micro-USD allowances; actual consumption or labeled estimates separate from provider usage, included credits, and verified charges.
safety_policy.workers: Bound publication tool only; no SQL, operator, or inspection-attestation tools exposed.

remaining_gates: Phase 4 full rejection/repair/review/exact-version director approval, stale approval and idempotent decisions, authenticated operator integration, bounded attempts/escalation and authorized extensions.
Full LangGraph checkpoint recovery; current tests prove SQL and artifact recovery only.
Phase 5 bounded concurrent production under provider limits.
Phase 6 film integration and verified migration/cutover; existing renderer and production runtime retained.
NVIDIA garbled-response reliability issue from Phase 2 remains unresolved; no provider substitution.
Crash tests use explicit isolated mocks and real SIGKILL, not live provider failures or hardware power loss.
complexity_review: Ponytail self-review: native SQLite, constraints and transactions; no ORM, new dependencies, queues, observability platform, dashboard, or generic workflow framework.
